claims.title: Molecular completion: consumptive signals, cis/trans delivery and renewal budgets

quoted_fields.interface: Actual product retention, chemical selectivity, donor clearance, cleavage topology, local delivery, fragment inactivation and end-group regeneration are separate operations. The supplied finite-state model assumes introduced k_cis, b, mu, c, alpha, W and correct fraction g; the one-use model additionally assumes permanently inactive fragments after the first cut. Uniform-sphere effective molarity is geometric, not a measured intramolecular rate.
quoted_fields.failure: A one-use key can still make its first cut on the wrong site. Faster indiscriminate trapping can destroy useful progression; stable sequestration is an alternative in the model rather than a demonstrated component. New source failures do not erase prior successful exposure or turn producer reports into ROOT governing reads. Per-event loss is distinct from per-cycle loss. Existing full-library, chemistry, assay, function, renewal and cost gaps remain open.
